title.en: State its properties and the reciprocal property

say.en: Two machines fill 1-litre milk packets. Both average 1 litre, but is one of them more erratic? To compare two variances we take their ratio, and that ratio follows the F distribution, named after R. A. Fisher. In this lesson: Define the F variate.
State its properties and the reciprocal property.
Relate t, χ squared and F.

body.en: If $\chi^2_1$ and $\chi^2_2$ are independent chi-square variates with $n_1$ and $n_2$ d.f., then $F = \dfrac{\chi^2_1/n_1}{\chi^2_2/n_2}$ follows the *F distribution* with $(n_1, n_2)$ d.f. For two independent samples from normal populations with equal variances, $F = s_1^2/s_2^2$ with $(n_1 - 1, n_2 - 1)$ d.f.
body.kn: ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ χ²₁ (n₁ d.f.) ಮತ್ತು χ²₂ (n₂ d.f.) ಆದರೆ F = (χ²₁/n₁)/(χ²₂/n₂) ಗೆ (n₁, n₂) ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ F ವಿತರಣೆ. ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ F = s₁²/s₂².

points.en: Ratio of two independent χ²s, each divided by its d.f.

For two independent samples from normal populations with equal variances, F = s_1^2/s_2^2 with (n_1 - 1, n_2 - 1) d.f.
narration.kn: ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ χ²₁ (n₁ d.f.) ಮತ್ತು χ²₂ (n₂ d.f.) ಆದರೆ F = (χ²₁/n₁)/(χ²₂/n₂) ಗೆ (n₁, n₂) ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ F ವಿತರಣೆ. ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ F = s₁²/s₂².

say.en: If chi-square 1 and chi-square 2 are independent chi-square variates with n 1 and n 2 d.f., then F equals dfracchi-square 1 over n 1chi-square 2 over n 2 follows the F distribution with (n 1, n 2) d.f. For two independent samples from normal populations with equal variances, F equals s 1 to the power 2 over s 2 to the power 2 with (n 1 minus 1, n 2 minus 1) d.f. Ratio of two independent χ squareds, each divided by its d.f.
say.kn: ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ χ squared 1 n 1 d.f. ಮತ್ತು χ squared 2 n 2 d.f. ಆದರೆ F equals (χ squared 1 over n 1)/(χ squared 2 over n 2) ಗೆ (n 1, n 2) ಸ್ವಾತಂತ್ರ್ಯ ಮಟ್ಟಗಳ F ವಿತರಣೆ. ಮಾದರಿಗಳಲ್ಲಿ F equals s 1 squared/s 2 squared.

Samples: F equals s 1 squared/s 2 squared.

say.en: F is a ratio of two independent chi-squares, each divided by its degrees of freedom.
Here is the F curve for 5 and 10 degrees of freedom. It starts at zero, rises and has a long right tail.
Its mean depends only on the denominator d.f.: n2 over n2 minus 2. For F(5, 10) that is 1.25.
Swap the d.f. and take the reciprocal: that gives the lower percentage point.
And t squared is F with 1 and n degrees of freedom.

title.en: The F distribution and its degrees of freedom

narration.en: F = (χ²₁/n₁)/(χ²₂/n₂) is never negative and is skewed to the right. Change the two degrees of freedom: the order matters, since F(n₁, n₂) and F(n₂, n₁) are different curves (turn on the dashed one). Its mean is n₂/(n₂ − 2), a little above 1.

say.en: F equals (χ squared 1 over n 1)/(χ squared 2 over n 2) is never negative and is skewed to the right. Change the two degrees of freedom: the order matters, since F(n 1, n 2) and F(n 2, n 1) are different curves turn on the dashed one. Its mean is n 2 over n 2 minus 2, a little above 1.

body.en: F ranges from 0 to $\infty$ and is positively skewed. Mean $= \dfrac{n_2}{n_2 - 2}$ ($n_2 > 2$). Reciprocal property: $F_{1-\alpha}(n_2, n_1) = 1/F_{\alpha}(n_1, n_2)$. Relations: $t_n^2 = F(1, n)$ and, as $n_2 \to \infty$, $n_1 F \to \chi^2_{n_1}$. Application: testing the equality of two population variances (and analysis of variance).
body.kn: F 0 ಯಿಂದ ∞, ಧನಾತ್ಮಕ ವಿಷಮ. ಸರಾಸರಿ n₂/(n₂ − 2). ವ್ಯುತ್ಕ್ರಮ ಗುಣ. t²ₙ = F(1, n). ಎರಡು ಪ್ರಸರಣಗಳ ಸಮಾನತೆಯ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಗೆ ಬಳಕೆ.

problem.en: The upper 5% point of F(5, 10) is 3.33. Find the lower 5% point of F(10, 5), and the mean of F(5, 10).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. The upper 5% point of F(5, 10) is 3.33. Find the lower 5% point of F(10, 5), and the mean of F(5, 10).

say.en: Let us work this out together. The upper 5 percent point of F(5, 10) is 3.33. Find the lower 5 percent point of F(10, 5), and the mean of F(5, 10).
Reciprocal property: F lower(10, 5) equals 1 over F upper(5, 10).
= 1 over 3.33 is approximately 0.30.
Mean of F(5, 10) equals 10 over 10 minus 2 equals 1.25.
So the answer is Lower point is approximately 0.30; mean 1.25.
